claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 can be processed to exhibit a well-defined hierarchical heterostructure.
The hierarchical heterostructure in HfNbTiVAl10 includes multiple phases, lamellar features, and distinct grain-boundary interfaces.
Quantitative descriptors of the heterostructure can be integrated into a multiscale homogenization framework for continuum-level prediction.
Phase interfaces, lamellar arrangements, and grain-boundary networks mediate elastic stiffness and localized yielding.
The mechanical contributions of the heterostructure span scales from nanoscale lamellae to coarser grain boundaries.
Representing spatially heterogeneous microstructural contributions allows the model to account for local stress-strain responses and interfacial load transfer.
Accounting for local stress-strain responses and interfacial load transfer reduces uncertainty in predicted elastic, yield, and fracture responses.
The hierarchical model will reduce prediction error for Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture-related parameters by roughly 20–30% relative to homogeneous simulations.
The hierarchical model will reduce computational time by about 50% relative to homogeneous simulations.
Established baseline simulations for this alloy treat it as a homogeneous medium without explicitly representing its hierarchical microstructure.
Non-reproducible microstructural heterogeneity could cause the hierarchical model to fail.
Impurities or extreme local stress concentrations can dominate the mechanical response and invalidate mean-field assumptions.
The model's improvement depends on the precision of microstructural characterization and the sensitivity of assumed interfacial properties.
The effect of heterogeneity on global mechanical response may be alloy-specific.
The proposed comparison will use independently measured Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness as reference outcomes.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if the hierarchical model does not achieve at least a 20% error reduction and approximately a 50% computation-time reduction relative to the homogeneous baseline.
